claim: Despite wide use, the effect of AI tools on real-world software development has not been well studied.
quote: Despite widespread adoption, the impact of AI tools on software development in the wild remains understudied.
counts_if: The retelling says the real-world effect of AI coding tools on developers has had little rigorous study so far.
contradicted_if: The retelling says the real-world effect of AI coding tools is already well established by prior research.

claim: The authors ran a randomized controlled trial to measure how early-2025 AI tools affect the productivity of experienced open-source developers.
quote: We conduct a randomized controlled trial (RCT) to understand how AI tools at the February-June 2025 frontier affect the productivity of experienced open-source developers.
counts_if: The retelling says the study was a randomized controlled experiment (or randomized trial) on experienced open-source developers using early-2025 AI tools.
contradicted_if: The retelling says the study was a survey, observational study, or lab benchmark with novices or non-randomized participants.

claim: Sixteen developers with moderate AI experience completed 246 tasks in mature projects they had worked on for about five years on average.
quote: 16 developers with moderate AI experience complete 246 tasks in mature projects on which they have an average of 5 years of prior experience.
counts_if: The retelling says a small group of about 16 experienced developers did a few hundred tasks in codebases they already knew well.
contradicted_if: The retelling says the participants were many hundreds of developers, beginners, or working on unfamiliar new codebases.

claim: Each task was randomly assigned to either allow or forbid the use of early-2025 AI tools.
quote: Each task is randomly assigned to allow or disallow usage of early 2025 AI tools.
counts_if: The retelling says that for each task it was decided at random whether the developer could use AI.
contradicted_if: The retelling says developers chose for themselves whether to use AI, or that the same developers always used AI.

claim: When AI was allowed, developers mainly used the Cursor Pro code editor and Claude 3.5/3.7 Sonnet.
quote: When AI tools are allowed, developers primarily use Cursor Pro, a popular code editor, and Claude 3.5/3.7 Sonnet.
counts_if: The retelling names Cursor and/or Claude Sonnet models as the main AI tools the developers used.
contradicted_if: The retelling says developers mainly used a different tool such as GitHub Copilot only or ChatGPT only.

claim: Before starting, developers predicted that allowing AI would cut their completion time by 24%.
quote: Before starting tasks, developers forecast that allowing AI will reduce completion time by 24%.
counts_if: The retelling says developers beforehand expected AI to make them substantially faster (roughly a quarter less time).
contradicted_if: The retelling says developers beforehand expected AI to slow them down or to make no difference.

claim: After the study, developers still believed that allowing AI had cut their completion time by 20%.
quote: After completing the study, developers estimate that allowing AI reduced completion time by 20%.
counts_if: The retelling says that even after the study developers believed AI had sped them up (roughly a fifth).
contradicted_if: The retelling says developers afterwards realized or believed that AI had slowed them down.

claim: Allowing AI actually made developers take 19% longer to complete tasks, so AI tools slowed them down.
quote: Surprisingly, we find that allowing AI actually increases completion time by 19%--AI tooling slowed developers down.
counts_if: The retelling says that in the study the developers were measurably slower (about a fifth longer) when allowed to use AI.
contradicted_if: The retelling says developers were faster with AI, or that AI made no measurable difference in the study.

claim: The measured slowdown contradicts the predictions of economics experts (39% faster) and machine learning experts (38% faster).
quote: This slowdown also contradicts predictions from experts in economics (39% shorter) and ML (38% shorter).
counts_if: The retelling says outside experts had predicted AI would speed developers up, and the result went against those predictions.
contradicted_if: The retelling says experts correctly predicted a slowdown, or that the result matched expert predictions.

claim: The authors examined evidence for 20 features of the study setting that could have contributed to the slowdown.
quote: we collect and evaluate evidence for 20 properties of our setting that a priori could contribute to the observed slowdown effect
counts_if: The retelling says the authors investigated a list of possible explanations (around 20 factors) for the slowdown.
contradicted_if: The retelling says the authors did not investigate any possible reasons for the slowdown.

claim: The factors examined included project size and quality standards and developers' prior experience with AI tools.
quote: for example, the size and quality standards of projects, or prior developer experience with AI tooling.
counts_if: The retelling mentions project size, quality standards, or developers' prior AI experience as factors the authors looked at.
contradicted_if: The retelling says the authors ruled out looking at project characteristics or developer AI experience.

claim: Experimental artifacts cannot be fully ruled out, but the slowdown held up across analyses and is unlikely to be mainly caused by the experimental design.
quote: Although the influence of experimental artifacts cannot be entirely ruled out, the robustness of the slowdown effect across our analyses suggests it is unlikely to primarily be a function of our experimental design.
counts_if: The retelling says the slowdown was robust and probably not just an artifact of how the experiment was set up, possibly with a caveat that artifacts cannot be entirely excluded.
contradicted_if: The retelling says the slowdown was most likely just an artifact of the experimental design, or that artifacts were fully ruled out.

claim: The authors caution readers not to overgeneralize from the results.
quote: We caution readers against overgeneralizing on the basis of our results.
counts_if: The retelling says the authors warn the findings should not be broadly generalized beyond the study setting.
contradicted_if: The retelling says the authors claim the result applies to all developers and all settings.

claim: The observed slowdown does not mean that current AI tools do not often improve developer productivity.
quote: The slowdown we observe does not imply that current AI tools do not often improve developer’s productivity
counts_if: The retelling says the result does not prove AI tools generally fail to help developers, or that AI often can still help.
contradicted_if: The retelling says the study shows AI coding tools generally do not improve productivity.

claim: There is evidence that developers' high familiarity with their repositories, and the repositories' size and maturity, contributed to the slowdown.
quote: we find evidence that the high developer familiarity with repositories and the size and maturity of the repositories both contribute to the observed slowdown
counts_if: The retelling says the slowdown was partly due to developers knowing their codebases well and/or the codebases being large and mature.
contradicted_if: The retelling says repository familiarity, size and maturity played no role or that the slowdown was unrelated to the codebase.

claim: The results are consistent with small new projects or unfamiliar codebases seeing substantial speedup from AI.
quote: our results are consistent with small greenfield projects or development in unfamiliar codebases seeing substantial speedup from AI assistance
counts_if: The retelling says AI might still substantially speed up work on small new projects or unfamiliar codebases.
contradicted_if: The retelling says the study shows AI also slows down work on small new projects or unfamiliar codebases.

claim: The authors expect that more reliable, lower-latency or better-prompted AI systems could speed up developers in this setting.
quote: could speed up developers in our setting (i.e. experienced open-source developers on large repositories)
counts_if: The retelling says improved or better-used AI systems might make these experienced developers faster in future.
contradicted_if: The retelling says the authors believe better AI systems could not help these developers.

claim: Preliminary evidence suggests fully autonomous AI agents using Claude 3.7 Sonnet can often implement the core functionality of issues in several of the study's repositories.
quote: We have preliminary evidence (forthcoming) that fully autonomous AI agents using Claude 3.7 Sonnet can often correctly implement the core functionality of issues on several repositories that are included in our study
counts_if: The retelling says early evidence shows autonomous AI agents can often get the main part of real issues in these repositories working.
contradicted_if: The retelling says AI agents cannot implement the core of these issues at all.

claim: Those AI agents typically fall short of meeting all requirements, for example leaving out documentation, failing style rules and missing key tests.
quote: although they fail to fully satisfy all requirements (typically leaving out important documentation, failing linting/styling rules, and leaving out key unit or integration tests)
counts_if: The retelling says the agents' work is incomplete, such as missing documentation, tests or style compliance.
contradicted_if: The retelling says the agents fully satisfy all requirements including documentation, style and tests.

claim: If AI progress continues, significant speedup may soon appear in this setting, though that is not guaranteed.
quote: if progress continues apace (which is a priori at least plausible, although not guaranteed), we may soon see significant speedup in this setting
counts_if: The retelling says continued AI progress could soon produce real speedups for these developers, without stating it as certain.
contradicted_if: The retelling says the authors are certain speedups will come, or that they believe speedups will never come.
